concepts.name: Platform
concepts.description: The overall platform encompasses every server-side and client-side service we ship, along with the shared infrastructure that ties them together; this description is intentionally long so that it overflows a standard 80-column terminal and demonstrates the new hard-wrapping behaviour at the root level where no branch indentation is consumed.

concepts.name: Backend
concepts.description: Core server-side services: HTTP request handling, background job processing, authentication, and persistence. Nested one level under Platform, so the branch prefix eats four columns and the wrapped text reflows into a slightly narrower box than the root description above it.

concepts.name: API
concepts.description:
Public and internal HTTP endpoints.
Design notes:
- versioned under /v1 and /v2
- rate limited per API key
- every long bullet line is wrapped independently so that manual newlines are preserved while still being clamped to the available width at this two-levels-deep position in the tree.

concepts.name: Database
concepts.description: Persistence and migrations. Three levels deep now, leaving even less horizontal room: the indentation grows by four columns per level, so this paragraph wraps into a visibly tighter column than its ancestors while still aligning its continuation lines under the branch.

concepts.name: Frontend
concepts.description: Browser-facing single-page application. A second root concept, used to confirm that wrapping is computed independently for each root subtree rather than sharing state across them.

concepts.name: Dashboard
concepts.description: User-facing metrics dashboard with charts, filters, and saved views; long enough to wrap one level under the Frontend root and show that continuation lines still line up with the tree branches.
